# DIAL — Dialectic Interagent Language v0.1 — Full Reference

DIAL is an XML language for structured performative exchange between any participants — humans, AI agents, systems, and services.
It encodes the pragmatic layer — what agents DO in exchange, not just what they say.
It is a superset of WUCE. WUCE's execution model lives inside <dial-execute>.

"Dialectic" is used in its classical sense: dia (through) + legein (to speak/reason).
Meaning arrived at THROUGH exchange. Not Hegelian opposition. Not two-party restricted.
The Socratic/Aristotelian tradition: reasoned discourse as the medium of understanding.

Intellectual lineage: Leibniz (characteristica universalis), Wittgenstein (meaning as use),
Austin/Searle (speech act theory / illocutionary force), Peirce (triadic sign), FIPA ACL.
What is new: LLMs can now produce well-formed DIAL naturally at runtime.

---

## 1. PROTOCOL REFERENCE

### Root element

<dial version="0.1" turn="{n}" actor="{human|agent|system|service}" session="{id}">
  ...elements...
</dial>

Attributes:
  version  — must be "0.1"
  turn     — 1-based turn index (optional)
  actor    — who produced this envelope
  session  — session id for context scoping (optional)

---

### Eight element types (parts of speech)

## <dial-inform>
An assertion. Delivers information. No response expected.

<dial-inform id="{id}" render="{prose|card-list|table|chart|code|media|map|diagram|raw}"
             observe="{event}" yield="{events}" addressed-to="{actor}">
  Natural language text OR <dial-payload type="application/json">...</dial-payload>
</dial-inform>

render values: prose (default), card-list, table, chart, code, media, map, diagram, raw

## <dial-ask>
An interrogative. Requests something. Blocking — gates elements that observe its yield.

<dial-ask id="{id}" response-type="{text|choice|confirm|number|file}" timeout="{seconds}"
          observe="{event}" yield="{events}" addressed-to="{actor}">
  Question text
  <dial-option value="{val}" default="{bool}" disabled="{bool}">Label</dial-option>
</dial-ask>

response-type values: text (default), choice, confirm, number, file
<dial-option> only used with response-type="choice"

## <dial-suggest>
A proposal. Non-blocking — exchange continues regardless of selection.

<dial-suggest id="{id}" render="{card-list|...}" action="{named-action}" multi="{bool}"
              observe="{event}" yield="{events}">
  <dial-payload type="application/json">[...]</dial-payload>
</dial-suggest>

Text content (outside any <dial-payload>) is optional: the human-readable proposal a receiver shows when asking
whether to take the action, e.g. <dial-suggest action="add-card">Add a Methodology card?</dial-suggest>.
Parsed as text, alongside payload.

## <dial-execute>
An imperative. Executes a step graph. Contains WUCE-style steps with observe/yield.
Steps carry raw executable commands — no translation layer, no abstract action types.
The AI emits the actual command; the executor runs it directly.

<dial-execute id="{id}" observe="{event}" yield="{events}">
  <step env="shell" id="{id}" label="{label}" observe="{event}" yield="{events}">
    command text
  </step>
  <step env="python" observe="{prior:event}" yield="{events}">
    python code or script path
  </step>
  <step env="http" yield="{events}">
    curl-style spec or JSON request descriptor
  </step>
</dial-execute>

step env values: shell (bash exec), python (python3), http (fetch), extensible
Steps without observe= run in parallel.
Steps with observe= wait for the named yield from a prior step.
Step yields are scoped inside <dial-execute>. The element itself yields to the outer envelope.

## <dial-acknowledge>
An affective. Signals receipt or understanding. No new information.

<dial-acknowledge id="{id}" of="{element-id}" observe="{event}" yield="{events}">
  Optional human-readable confirmation text
</dial-acknowledge>

## <dial-declare>
A declaration. Asserts a named fact into shared session context.
Future elements in this or subsequent turns may reference it by context-key.

<dial-declare id="{id}" context-key="{key}" observe="{event}" yield="{events}">
  <dial-payload type="application/json">...</dial-payload>
</dial-declare>

Note: XML attribute is context-key (kebab). In parsed JS: el.contextKey (camelCase).

## <dial-delegate>
A handoff. Transfers responsibility to another actor.

<dial-delegate id="{id}" to="{actor-id}" intent="{named-intent}" resume="{bool}"
               observe="{event}" yield="{events}">
  Optional description
  <dial-context>
    <dial-payload type="application/json">...</dial-payload>
  </dial-context>
</dial-delegate>

## <dial-phatic>
A channel signal. No semantic payload. Typing indicators, heartbeats, presence.

<dial-phatic signal="{typing|thinking|heartbeat|presence|done-typing}" interval="{seconds}" />

---

### Common attributes on all elements

id="{string}"           — unique within envelope (auto-assigned if omitted)
observe="{event-name}"  — activates only when this event is yielded by another element
yield="{event-names}"   — space-separated events emitted when this element resolves
addressed-to="{actor}"  — target actor id; omit = broadcast
lang="{bcp47}"          — language tag for natural language content (default: "en")

---

### Child elements

<dial-payload type="application/json" encoding="utf-8" schema="{uri}">
  Structured data container. Used when content is not natural language text.
</dial-payload>

<dial-option value="{string}" default="{bool}" disabled="{bool}">
  Label text
</dial-option>
Used only inside <dial-ask response-type="choice">.

---

### Observe/yield — two nested scopes

Outer scope (DIAL envelope): element dependencies
Inner scope (inside <dial-execute>): step dependencies

Example:
<dial version="0.1" actor="agent">
  <dial-ask id="q1" response-type="confirm" yield="confirmed cancelled" />

  <dial-execute id="op1" observe="confirmed" yield="op:done op:failed">
    <step env="shell" id="a" yield="a:done">ls -la /path</step>
    <step env="shell" id="b" observe="a:done" yield="b:done">cat /path/README.md</step>
  </dial-execute>

  <dial-inform id="result" observe="op:done" render="prose">
    Operation completed.
  </dial-inform>
</dial>

Outer: dial-ask → confirmed → dial-execute → op:done → dial-inform
Inner: step-a → a:done → step-b → b:done
Inner step yields are invisible to the outer scope.

---

### Key rules

- Elements without observe= activate immediately, in parallel
- Elements with observe= wait for the named yield from another element
- <dial-ask> is blocking — nothing that observes its yield runs until human responds
- <dial-suggest> is non-blocking — selection events available but exchange doesn't wait
- <dial-declare> values are accessible by context-key in subsequent turns
- Any number of parties may participate — DIAL is not restricted to two actors
- A <dial> envelope with only <dial-execute> is valid — compatible with WUCE

---

### WUCE compatibility

WUCE v2.3 steps map to DIAL <step> as follows:
  stepName                              → id
  stepDescription / stepMsg            → label
  actionDomain + actionType + actionMeta → env + text content (raw command)
  observe                              → observe (identical)
  yield                                → yield (identical)
  observationDomain                    → dropped (subsumed by env)

Every valid WUCE envelope is a valid <dial-execute> block.

---

## 2. JAVASCRIPT PACKAGE — @wity.ai/dial

npm install @wity.ai/dial

Built on dial-core (Rust/WASM). WASM is pre-built and bundled — no Rust toolchain needed
for consumers. Two entry points auto-selected by toolchain via package.json exports conditions.

### Environment matrix

  Environment        | Entry point          | parse() / extractProse()
  -------------------|----------------------|-----------------------------
  Node.js            | index.js             | Synchronous
  Browser/Vite/webpack | index.browser.js   | Async (Promise) — WASM via fetch
  CommonJS (require) | index.cjs            | Synchronous

Vite picks up the "browser" export condition automatically. Node.js uses "node" condition.
No bundler config or aliases needed.

---

### Node.js usage

import { parse, extractProse, DialSession, DialRouter, runStepGraph } from '@wity.ai/dial';

// Parse a DIAL envelope from AI response text (may contain surrounding prose)
const envelope = parse(aiText);              // DialEnvelope | null
const prose    = extractProse(aiText);       // string — text outside <dial> blocks

const session = new DialSession();
const router  = new DialRouter()
  .on('dial-inform',  (el, ctx) => {
    // el.render, el.text, el.payload
  })
  .on('dial-ask',     async (el, ctx) => {
    // el.responseType, el.options, el.timeout
    ctx.emit('choice:yes');                  // yield an event programmatically
  })
  .on('dial-execute', async (el, ctx) => {
    const { results } = await runStepGraph(el.steps, async (step) => {
      const output = await exec(step.command);
      return { command: step.command, env: step.env, stdout: output, success: true };
    });
    ctx.session.recordResults(results);
  })
  .on('dial-declare', (el, ctx) => {
    if (el.contextKey) ctx.session.declare(el.contextKey, el.payload ?? el.text);
  })
  .on('dial-suggest', (el, ctx) => {
    // el.action, el.render, el.payload (array of option objects)
  })
  .on('dial-delegate', async (el, ctx) => {
    // el.to, el.intent, el.payload (context for receiving actor)
  });

if (envelope) await router.route(envelope, session);

---

### Browser usage (Vite + vanilla JS)

import { parse, extractProse, initDial, DialSession, DialRouter, runStepGraph }
  from '@wity.ai/dial';

// Optional: pre-load WASM at app startup to avoid cold-start latency on first parse()
// If omitted, parse() auto-initialises on first call.
await initDial();

const session = new DialSession();
const router  = new DialRouter()
  .on('dial-inform',  (el, ctx) => { /* update DOM */ })
  .on('dial-declare', (el, ctx) => {
    if (el.contextKey) ctx.session.declare(el.contextKey, el.payload ?? el.text);
  });

chatWidget.onNewMessage(async (text) => {
  const envelope = await parse(text);        // await — async in browser build
  if (envelope) await router.route(envelope, session);
});

// extractProse is also async in browser build:
const prose = await extractProse(text);

---

### API reference

#### parse(text: string) → DialEnvelope | null  [Node]
#### parse(text: string) → Promise<DialEnvelope | null>  [Browser]
Parses the first <dial> envelope found in text. Returns null if none present.
Input may contain surrounding prose — only the structured block is extracted and parsed.

#### extractProse(text: string) → string  [Node]
#### extractProse(text: string) → Promise<string>  [Browser]
Returns text outside any <dial> block. Useful for rendering the natural language
portion of a mixed response alongside DIAL-driven UI.

#### initDial() → Promise<void>  [Browser only]
Pre-loads the WASM binary via fetch. Safe to call multiple times (fetch happens once).
Call at app startup to eliminate cold-start latency on the first parse().

#### new DialSession(opts?: { maxResults?: number })
Per-session state container. Two orthogonal streams:
  .declare(key: string, value: unknown) → void
      Store a declared context value (from handling <dial-declare>).
  .getDeclared() → Record<string, unknown>
      Defensive snapshot of all declared context.
  .recordResults(results: DialExecutionResult[]) → void
      Append execution results. Rolling window (default: last 10, configurable via maxResults).
  .getLastResults() → DialExecutionResult[]
      Defensive snapshot of recent execution results.
  .clear() → void
      Reset all state (declared + results).

#### new DialRouter()
Dispatches elements from a parsed envelope to registered handlers, respecting
the observe/yield dependency graph. Handlers for unknown types are silently skipped.

  .on(type: string, handler: ElementHandler) → this   (chainable)
  .route(envelope: DialEnvelope, session: DialSession) → Promise<void>

ElementHandler: (el: DialElementNode, ctx: RouteContext) => Promise<void> | void
RouteContext: { session: DialSession, emit: (event: string) => void }

ctx.emit(event) — yield an event programmatically from inside a handler.
Used by dial-ask handlers to signal which choice/confirm outcome occurred,
allowing downstream elements that observe those events to activate.

#### runStepGraph(steps, executor, initialYielded?) → Promise<{ results, yielded }>
Runs the inner observe/yield dependency loop for a <dial-execute> step array.
Use inside a 'dial-execute' handler to sequence steps correctly.

  steps         — el.steps from a DialElementNode of type 'dial-execute'
  executor      — async (step: DialStepNode) => DialExecutionResult
  initialYielded — optional Set<string> of pre-yielded event names

Returns:
  results — DialExecutionResult[] in completion order
  yielded — Set<string> of all events yielded by the step graph

---

### TypeScript shapes

// Parsed envelope (return value of parse())
interface DialEnvelope {
  attributes: { version?: string; turn?: number; actor?: string; session?: string };
  elements:   DialElementNode[];
  raw:        string;
}

// Element node (union of all element types via discriminated `type` field)
interface DialElementNode {
  type:         string;          // 'dial-inform' | 'dial-ask' | 'dial-execute' | etc.
  id?:          string;
  observe?:     string;
  yield?:       string[];
  addressedTo?: string;
  // dial-inform / dial-declare / dial-phatic (signal in text?)
  render?:      string;
  text?:        string;
  payload?:     unknown;
  // dial-ask
  responseType?: string;
  timeout?:      number;
  options?:      DialOption[];
  // dial-execute
  steps?:       DialStepNode[];
  // dial-suggest (its `text` is the human-readable proposal)
  action?:      string;
  // dial-declare
  contextKey?:  string;          // XML: context-key → JS: contextKey (camelCase)
  // dial-acknowledge
  of?:          string;
  // dial-phatic
  signal?:      string;
  // dial-delegate
  to?:          string;
  intent?:      string;
}

interface DialStepNode {
  env:      string;    // 'shell' | 'python' | 'http' | custom
  id?:      string;
  label?:   string;
  observe?: string;
  yield?:   string[];
  command:  string;    // raw command — AI emits this directly
}

interface DialOption {
  value:   string;
  label:   string;
  default: boolean;
}

// Consumer-facing element — what the wity-chat widget delivers via onDialEvent.
// Omits routing internals that the widget resolves before emission.
type DialEventElement = Omit<DialElementNode, 'observe' | 'yield' | 'timeout' | 'steps'>;

interface DialExecutionResult {
  command: string;
  env:     string;
  stdout:  string;
  stderr:  string;
  success: boolean;
  error?:  string;
}

---

### Build targets (contributors / monorepo)

The WASM is built via wasm-pack from packages/dial-core-wasm (Rust):

  npm run build:wasm:node   # --target nodejs  → pkg-node/ (synchronous fs loader)
  npm run build:wasm:web    # --target web     → pkg-web/  (async fetch loader)
  npm run build             # both

pkg-node/ is consumed by the Node.js entry (parse.js via createRequire).
pkg-web/ is consumed by the browser entry (parse.browser.js — lazy async init, cached).

After build:wasm:web, pkg-web/package.json name is auto-patched to "dial-core-wasm-web"
to avoid collision with the pkg-node package in node_modules.

Both are included in bundleDependencies — the published @wity.ai/dial tarball is self-contained.

---

### Knowledge persistence — @wity/dial-knowledge (separate package)

import { KnowledgeStore, FileAdapter } from '@wity/dial-knowledge';

Provides cross-session persistence of declared context and execution results.
Separate concern from the protocol layer — not included in @wity.ai/dial.

---

## 3. CONSUMER RUNTIME — @wity.ai/dial-runtime

In this repository: packages/dial-runtime. Not yet published to the public npm registry. Depends on @wity.ai/dial.
Runs one conversation with an agent that speaks DIAL: the turn loop, and the life of each proposal the agent makes
(validated, shown readable, accepted / dismissed / edited by a person, run, reported back). Domain-agnostic: a
domain supplies the actions; a surface (terminal, chat panel, test) shows the conversation and plays the person.
Adds nothing to the DIAL schema.

### Usage

import { Conversation, NoReplyError, outcomeReply, policyHuman, scriptedHuman } from '@wity.ai/dial-runtime';

const conversation = new Conversation({
  agent:  { send: async (message) => replyText },
  domain: { actions, validate, preview, run, context },
  human:  { decide: async (suggestion) => ({ accept: true }), answer: async (ask) => 'yes' },
  onEvent: (event) => {},        // optional
  timeoutMs: 90000,              // default — how long the agent may take to reply
  maxTurns: 8,                   // default — turns one say() may use
});

const { status, turns, outcomes } = await conversation.say('add a note: buy milk');
  status 'idle'       — the last reply needed nothing back
  status 'no-reply'   — the agent did not answer within timeoutMs
  status 'turn-limit' — maxTurns were used
If agent.send rejects for another reason, say() rejects with that error.

### One turn

Sent, in order: the outcomes of the previous turn (if any) · domain.context() · the person's words.
The reply is parsed; its elements are handled in order:
  <dial-inform>, <dial-acknowledge> → event 'inform' (act: 'inform' | 'acknowledge')
  <dial-ask>                        → event 'ask', then human.answer(ask); the answer goes on the next turn.
                                      An empty answer means the question stands: no turn follows.
  <dial-suggest>                    → a suggestion (below)
A reply with no <dial> envelope is emitted as 'inform' text; so is prose outside the envelope.
A suggestion's payload is the <dial-suggest>'s own <dial-payload>; if it has none, the <dial-declare> that
immediately follows it is taken as its payload.

### The life of a suggestion — every one ends in exactly one outcome

  unknown action / payload refused by domain.validate → invalid   (the person never sees it; carries code, field, hint)
  read-only action (mutates: false)                    → runs at once → done | failed
  hand-off action (handoff: true)                      → runs at once → handed-off
  otherwise human.decide(suggestion):
      { accept: true }   → runs → done | failed
      { edit: payload }  → validated (a refused edit is shown back as suggestion.issue and decided again;
                           after three refused edits → invalid), then runs → done | failed (edited: true)
      { dismiss: true }  → dismissed
      { say: text }      → superseded — this and the reply's remaining suggestions; the words go with the next turn

Only done / failed / invalid make a turn follow at once. dismissed / superseded / handed-off are reported with the
person's next words — a dismissal alone starts no turn.
What the agent was not told (a send failed, or no reply) is kept and goes with the next say(): the outcomes, and
words the person gave inside the conversation. say('') sends just what is owed.

A suggestion's id is the <dial-suggest>'s id when given, otherwise sg-1, sg-2, …

### Outcome replies — outcomeReply(outcomes)

<dial>
  <dial-acknowledge of="sg-3" yield="sg-3:failed">Couldn't do it: Add 'Brand' to Strengths.</dial-acknowledge>
  <dial-declare context-key="outcome:sg-3">
    <dial-payload type="application/json">{"action":"matrix.entry.add","status":"failed","error":"…","hint":"…"}</dial-payload>
  </dial-declare>
</dial>

Statuses: done · failed · invalid · dismissed · superseded · handed-off
Payload: action, status, and by status — result (what the action returned), error, code, field, hint, edited.

### Domain

{
  actions:  { 'add-note': { mutates: true }, 'remove-note': { mutates: true, destructive: true },
              'list-notes': { mutates: false }, 'open-poll': { mutates: false, handoff: true } },
  validate: (action, payload) => ({ ok: true }) | ({ ok: false, code, field?, hint }),
  preview:  (action, payload) => "Add the note 'buy milk'",   // what the person is shown; falls back to the action name
  run:      (action, payload) => result,                       // may be async; a thrown error → failed (message, code?, field?, hint?)
  context:  () => string,                                      // sent with every turn, or ''
}

### Human

{ decide: async (suggestion) => { accept: true } | { dismiss: true } | { edit: payload } | { say: text },
  answer: async (ask) => string }                              // '' or null = no answer

suggestion: { id, action, text, payload, preview, destructive } (+ issue after a refused edit) — text is the
agent's own wording from the <dial-suggest>.   ask: { text, responseType, options }

policyHuman('accept' | 'dismiss', { answerWith })  — the same decision every time
scriptedHuman(['accept', 'dismiss', { edit: {…} }, { say: '…' }, { answer: '…' }])  — in order

### Events — onEvent(event)

  sent        { turn, message }
  reply       { turn, text }
  inform      { text, act? }
  ask         { text, responseType, options }
  suggestion  { id, action, text, payload, preview, destructive, mutates }   — valid suggestions only
  outcome     { id, action, status, preview, …the outcome's fields }
  no-reply    { turn, error }
  turn-limit  { turns }

### Environments
Runs wherever @wity.ai/dial's parser does: parse() is synchronous in Node.js and returns a Promise in the browser;
the runtime awaits both.
